title: Tenant consent & maintenance lifecycle — draft playbook
body:
Purpose:
This draft documents a customer-consent-first maintenance and upgrade communication lifecycle for Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) customers. It combines: communication templates, consent collection patterns, a simple escalation matrix, and a set of small Terraform module annotations that ops/SEs can add to customer stacks to make scheduling and metadata explicit. The goal: minimize surprise, protect SLA/SLO commitments, and make automated scheduling pipelines auditable.

Scope and assumptions:
- Audience: solutions engineering, SRE, customer success, account managers for private deployments.
- Applies to planned maintenance events and non-urgent rolling upgrades (kernel/OS, infra agents, Redwood runtime updates).
- Major model or data migrations that require longer customer verification are out-of-scope and use a separate migration playbook.
- Customers can be in three consent tiers: Opt-in (explicit consent required), Opt-out (we schedule but notify), and Emergency-exempt (critical security fixes).

Quick overview of flow (concise):
1) Pre-notify (T-minus 14 days): high-level scope, expected downtime/impact window, preliminary SLO impact estimate. Consent request if customer is Opt-in.
2) Reminder (T-minus 7 days): confirm date/time or collect reschedule requests.
3) Final reminder (T-minus 48 hours): operational runbook, contact numbers, temporary mitigations.
4) Maintenance execution: live Slack channel, progress updates every 30–60 minutes.
5) Post-maintenance (T+24 hours): results, incident/resolution summary, remediation items, and ask for customer verification.

Communication templates (editable):
A) High-level email (T-14) — Subject: Redwood Private maintenance window request — [Customer org]
Hi [Customer Owner],

We are planning a maintenance/update to the Redwood Private runtime that affects your deployment in [region/cluster]. Proposed window: [YYYY-MM-DD from hh:mm to hh:mm timezone].

Summary:
- Purpose: [short reason, e.g., security patch, performance improvements]
- Expected customer impact: [none / <1% request latency increase / brief restart of control-plane pods / rolling worker restarts with no request loss]
- SLO impact estimate: [Expected 0.2% additional error rate across window; no change to availability SLO].

Action required:
- If you are on Opt-in consent tier, please reply YES to approve or REQUEST RESCHEDULE with a preferred window by [YYYY-MM-DD].
- If we do not hear back by [YYYY-MM-DD (7 days from now)], we will automatically schedule the maintenance per your tier.

Contact: [SE name], [email], phone: [x].

Thanks,
Redwood Private Operations

B) Reminder (T-7) — Slack DM / Email snippet:
Reminder: upcoming Redwood maintenance for [customer]. Please confirm availability or mark a preferred alternative. Link to change request: [link].

C) Final reminder (T-48 hours) — Subject: Final notice: Redwood maintenance in 48 hours
Hello [Customer Owner],

Final confirmation for maintenance window on [date/time]. Please ensure any in-flight jobs are paused by [time]. The maintenance is expected to be rolling and non-disruptive to inference traffic; however control-plane restarts may briefly disrupt administrative actions (failover is automatic).

If you need to change the window, reply with REQUEST RESCHEDULE and one or two alternative windows within next 24 hours.

Operational contact: [phone / channel link].

D) In-progress update (use in Slack channel and email digest every 30–60m):
- [timestamp] Step: draining worker X in zone Y — ETA 12m
- [timestamp] Completed: drained worker X, started kernel update
- Current customer impact: [none / degraded API ttfb on worker Y]

E) Post-maintenance report (T+24) — Subject: Redwood maintenance complete — [date]
Summary:
- Completed steps: [bulleted list]
- Observed impact vs predicted: [latency spikes, error counts, other metrics]
- Rollback performed? [no / yes — reason]
- Follow-ups: [ticket numbers, remediation actions, ETA]

Please reply with CONFIRM if your team observed no regressions. If you report any issues within 7 days, we will prioritize a follow-up run and include a targeted rollback if required.

Consent tiers and treatment rules (short):
- Opt-in: maintenance requires explicit approver reply (owner or delegated admin). We will not proceed without explicit YES.
- Opt-out: we schedule after T-14 notice; customers may reschedule until T-2.
- Emergency-exempt: immediate critical fixes; we notify as soon as practical and start remediation.

Rescheduling rules and cooldowns:
- First reschedule accepted up to T-2; subsequent reschedules limited to two per calendar quarter.
- Large reschedule requests (more than 7 days range change) require SE approval and may trigger a localized blackout calendar.

SLA/SLO impact shorthand and messaging guidance:
- Always state estimate and confidence band (e.g., 0.2% ± 0.1% error budget consumption).
- Default wording for low impact: "No expected change to availability SLO; minor transient latency increases possible during worker restarts."
- If SLO impact >0.5% or more than 1 minute p95 latency delta: route to account manager and legal for joint customer notice draft.

Escalation matrix (for customer-facing incidents during maintenance):
- Tier 1 (first 30 minutes): on-call SRE + SE assigned to customer; internal Slack #pd-maintenance-live; phone bridge if customer requests.
- Tier 2 (30–120 minutes unresolved): Eng lead paged; prepare rollback plan; account manager notified.
- Tier 3 (120+ minutes or customer business-impacting): Exec on-call notified; legal and security briefed; consider urgent rollback.

Terraform module annotations (notes to include in customer stacks):
These are small optional metadata variables to emit into Terraform state or resource tags so automation can gather scheduling constraints from the customer repo. The goal is to avoid back-and-forth and let customers express constraints declaratively. Example semantic suggestions (copy/paste friendly text):

# terraform snippet (plain text — add into customer module variables)
variable "maintenance_window_preferences" {
  description = "JSON string; fields: preferred_days, blackout_ranges, contact_emails, consent_tier"
  type        = string
  default     = "{\"preferred_days\": [\"wed\", \"thu\"], \"blackout_ranges\": [], \"contact_emails\": [\"ops@example.com\"], \"consent_tier\": \"opt-out\"}"
}

# recommended module tag mapping
resource "redwood_private_deployment" "this" {
  name = var.deployment_name
  tags = merge(var.tags, { "rw_maintenance_contact" = join(",", jsondecode(var.maintenance_window_preferences).contact_emails) })
}

Operational notes for teams adding the above snippet:
- Keep the JSON small — only the fields we need for automated scheduling. Do not store secrets.
- When generating notices, the scheduler will prefer preferred_days and avoid blackout_ranges. If consent_tier == opt-in, scheduler will create a human approval ticket instead of auto-scheduling.
- For on-prem airgapped installs where Terraform is not available, provide an equivalent YAML metadata file in the customer repo (repo path: /redwood/ops/maintenance-metadata.yaml).

Runbook checklist (for the executing SRE/SE pair):
- [ ] Confirm final ticket and runbook in internal system
- [ ] Confirm contact list + phone bridge established
- [ ] Verify backup snapshots taken (control-plane, DB metadata) — store location and retention
- [ ] Verify Terraform annotation presence or that customer provided metadata
- [ ] Run canary node first, validate metrics for 15m
- [ ] Proceed with rolling update, update runbook timestamps for each zone
- [ ] If unexpected error > defined threshold (increase in 5xx by 1% or queue growth > 20%), pause and escalate per matrix

Customer portal UI copy (short, for product to show maintenance card):
Title: Upcoming maintenance — Redwood runtime
When: [date/time]
Impact: [Low / Medium / High]
Action: [If Opt-in, Approve / Decline] [If Opt-out, Request reschedule]
Notes: Contact [SE name] or open support ticket #PD-UPGRADE-1289

Special cases and guidance:
- Airgapped customers — prefer asynchronous notifications (email + portal) and require a single human approver. Validate that KMS rotations do not overlap.
- Regulated customers (PCI/healthcare) — include legal and compliance in T-14 notice; allow 7 business days for consent for any runtime change that may show data flow changes.
- Zero-downtime upgrades: call out exactly what validates the zero-downtime claim (eg: rolling worker drains, no model reloads). If claim cannot be met, escalate and treat as a higher-impact change.

Post-maintenance verification checklist (ask customer to run):
- [ ] Basic inference sanity check with 3 example requests
- [ ] Internal admin console access verified
- [ ] Any scheduled batch jobs observed to run normally after the maintenance window

Template: internal postmortem blurb (short) — add to internal incident page:
Summary: planned maintenance completed on [date]. Impact: [none|minor|major]. Root cause: n/a (planned). Actions: tighten pre-checks for job scheduling; add telemetry to flag node warm-up.

Open items / discussion points for team review (editable):
- Do we want to push customers into a single canonical consent interface (portal) or keep email as a valid legal opt-in?
- Should Terraform annotation include timezone preference explicitly (customer still requests windows in local TZ)?
- How to surface predicted SLO impact more quantitatively from the staging telemetry?

Notes for legal / account teams:
- For Opt-in customers, treat a lack of reply as explicit DENY only if consent window stated that no reply == deny. Default in this playbook: no-reply toggles to scheduling behavior based on consent_tier (opt-in blocks, opt-out proceeds).
- Keep a copy of all customer approvals attached to the upgrade CR for audit.

Appendix: sample short approval reply (customer-facing)
YES — Approve maintenance on [date/time]. Contact: [name, email].
REQUEST RESCHEDULE — Prefer [two alternative date/time windows].

End — this doc is intended as a living draft. Questions / edits: ping #pd-maintenance-feedback or add comments in the linked Confluence page.
